summary: Provides a user-mediated JSON meal intake flow and a first reporting slice with two independent column charts over nutritional data, server-side bucket aggregation, and scope/drill navigation — all over the existing foodtracker.food_logs table.

classification.why_application: FoodTracker encodes domain-specific meaning across both sprints: meal intake validation rules, nutritional field semantics, dish_name derivation, bucket-generation logic keyed to nutrition domain concepts (kcal, protein_g, etc.), and drill-navigation behaviour specific to this reporting UX. None of this belongs in a shared platform capability.
non_goals: Prefetching or background loading of non-visible report states
Client-side aggregation from a full raw-data cache
User-local timezone handling (server time used for this slice)
classification.not_platform: Aggregation logic, bucket-generation rules, zero-fill behaviour, and drill-navigation state are all specific to the FoodTracker nutrition domain. Bucket semantics (year/month/week/day keyed to kcal/protein_g/carbs_g/fat_g/fiber_g) carry domain meaning and must not be promoted to a shared platform service.

consumes: 02_Platform/01_Postgres — Postgres instance on atlas-net reachable via ATLAS_PG_HOST:ATLAS_PG_PORT
02_Platform/UI — apiFetch, isApiError, ErrorCard, Skeleton platform UI primitives
provides: GET /api/food/template → text/plain canonical JSON template string
POST /api/food/meals → Dataset (HTTP 200, one row) or ApiError (HTTP 400 / 422 / 500)
GET /api/food/report → Dataset (HTTP 200, N bucket rows) or ApiError (HTTP 400 / 422 / 500)
Shell route /food registered under appId 'food' with nav items 'Log' (order 1) and 'Report' (order 2)
invariants: No row is written to foodtracker.food_logs unless the user has explicitly clicked Accept (POST /api/food/meals)
No draft or intermediate state is persisted to the database at any point
The commit endpoint re-validates the payload independently — it never relies on prior validate call results
The preview reflects the normalised data that will be written; it is not a rendering of the raw JSON
dish_name is always derived server-side by joining items[].name with ', '
kcal is always cast to integer (rounded) before insert and preview
confidence defaults to 3 when absent; all optional numeric nutrition fields default to 0 when absent
The report endpoint is strictly read-only — it never writes to foodtracker.food_logs
The report response always contains all five metric columns (kcal, protein_g, carbs_g, fat_g, fiber_g) in every row regardless of which metric is displayed

Zero-value bucket rows are generated for every date/period in the selected scope with no logged entries, ensuring a complete and stable x-axis — EXCEPT for (a) scope=all_time with mode=daily, where no enumerable period boundary exists; in that case only DB result rows are returned (no zero-fill), and an empty dataset is returned when no rows exist; and (b) scope=all_time with mode=aggregated, where bucket ids are the distinct years present in the DB result; only years with data are returned (no synthetic zero-fill for years with no data)
week scope always returns daily mode only; aggregated mode is rejected for week scope with a validation error
Bucket id values are stable identifiers for the bucket (e.g., '2025-03-01' for daily, '2025-03' for month, '2025-W12' for week, '2025' for year)
Backend owns all aggregation — the frontend never computes aggregated metrics from raw rows
failure_modes: PARSE_ERROR — request body is not syntactically valid JSON; HTTP 422 (intake endpoints only)
MISSING_FIELD — a required top-level or nutrition field is absent; HTTP 422 (intake endpoints only)
INVALID_FIELD — a field is present but fails type or constraint checks; HTTP 422
VALIDATION_ERROR — wrapper code for all validate/commit validation failures; HTTP 422
INVALID_PARAM — a query parameter for GET /api/food/report is missing, has an invalid value, or is an incompatible combination (e.g. mode=aggregated with scope=week); HTTP 422
INVALID_PERIOD_KEY — period_key format does not match the expected pattern for the given scope; HTTP 422
DB_CONSTRAINT — a database CHECK constraint is violated at insert time; HTTP 400 (intake only)
INTERNAL_ERROR — unexpected exception caught by install_exception_handlers; HTTP 500

consumes: platform_contracts.ColumnSchema, DatasetMeta, Dataset for commit and report responses
provides: HTTP API on port 8012 (container port 8000, host-bound to 127.0.0.1:8012)
Shell routes /food and /food/report consumed by 02_Platform/02_Atlas_Shell router

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/food/template
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Returns the hardcoded canonical meal JSON template as text/plain so the frontend can display it in a selectable read-only area for the user to copy.

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/food/validate
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Accepts a raw JSON payload, runs all validation checks, normalises the data, and returns the preview model on success or ApiError on any failure. No database write. food.py is unchanged in Sprint 02; this surface is declared here for completeness. The governing contract artifact for this sprint remains the Sprint 01 definition.
exposed_surfaces.ui_contract: preview_model (shape: {preview: <normalised_dict>}; field definitions governed by 00_Requirements/FoodTracker01 — Manual JSON Intake.md §6.4) | ApiError

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/food/meals
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Accepts the same raw JSON payload as validate, re-runs full validation and normalisation, inserts one row into foodtracker.food_logs, and returns the inserted row as a Dataset with MEAL_SCHEMA.

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/food/report
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Accepts scope, period_key (optional for all_time), and mode query parameters. Queries foodtracker.food_logs, applies server-side aggregation and zero-fill bucket generation, and returns a Dataset where each row is one time bucket containing all five metric columns.

internal_flow.name: receive_raw_body (intake)
internal_flow.description: FastAPI receives the request body as raw bytes and attempts JSON decode. If decode fails, raises PARSE_ERROR immediately. Applies to POST /api/food/validate and POST /api/food/meals only.

internal_flow.name: validate_fields (intake)
internal_flow.description: Sequential field validation: timestamp parseable as ISO-8601, meal_type in allowed enum, items non-empty array with non-empty name strings, nutrition object present, required numeric fields present and >= 0, optional numeric fields satisfy their individual >= 0 checks if present, cross-field constraints checked after both operand fields pass, confidence is integer 1-5 if present. Returns first failure. Failure signaled by return value, not exception.
outputs: (normalised_dict, None) on success or (None, error_dict) on failure

internal_flow.name: normalise (intake)
internal_flow.description: Apply defaults (fiber_g, good_fat_g, meat_g, red_meat_g, sodium_mg → 0; confidence → 3), derive dish_name by joining items[].name with ', ', cast kcal to int, re-serialise timestamp as 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS', strip unknown fields.

internal_flow.name: return_preview_or_insert (intake)
internal_flow.description: For POST /api/food/validate: return the normalised preview dict (HTTP 200). For POST /api/food/meals: proceed to DB insert.
outputs: preview model response (validate) or proceeds to step 5 (meals)

internal_flow.name: db_insert (intake)
internal_flow.description: Generate uuid4 for id. Execute INSERT INTO foodtracker.food_logs with all normalised field values. RETURNING * to retrieve the inserted row. Catch psycopg2.IntegrityError or CheckViolation and raise DB_CONSTRAINT ApiError (HTTP 400). Commit on success.
outputs: inserted row dict or DB_CONSTRAINT ApiError

internal_flow.name: build_dataset_response (intake)
internal_flow.description: Wrap the inserted row in a Dataset using MEAL_SCHEMA and DatasetMeta(object_type='food_meal', label='Food Log', total=1, page=1, page_size=1, row_actions=[]). Serialise id and logged_at as strings; all numeric fields as float.

internal_flow.name: validate_report_params (report)
internal_flow.description: Parse and validate query parameters for GET /api/food/report: scope must be one of all_time|year|month|week; period_key must be omitted for all_time or match the expected format for other scopes (YYYY for year, YYYY-MM for month, YYYY-WNN for week); mode must be aggregated|daily; mode=aggregated is rejected for scope=week with INVALID_PARAM. Returns a structured ReportQuery value object on success or ApiError (HTTP 422) on any failure.
outputs: ReportQuery value object or INVALID_PARAM/INVALID_PERIOD_KEY ApiError

internal_flow.name: compute_bucket_boundaries (report)
internal_flow.description: From the validated ReportQuery, compute the complete ordered list of expected bucket ids covering the selected period. For daily mode: enumerate every calendar day in the period — EXCEPT for scope=all_time where no period boundary can be determined from the query alone; in that case return an empty bucket list and skip zero-fill (the DB result rows are returned as-is without zero-fill). For aggregated mode: enumerate sub-period labels per the bucket rules (all_time+aggregated→distinct years present in the db_rows input, year+aggregated→months, month+aggregated→weeks). For scope=all_time+aggregated, the DB query (step 9) must run before this step so that db_rows is available; _compute_buckets accepts an optional db_rows parameter that is required (non-None) for this case. This list is used later to zero-fill missing buckets.
inputs: db_rows: dict[str, dict] | None (required for scope=all_time+aggregated; None for all other scope+mode combinations)

internal_flow.name: query_food_logs (report)
internal_flow.description: Execute a SELECT with GROUP BY against foodtracker.food_logs to aggregate kcal, protein_g, carbs_g, fat_g, fiber_g within the selected period. Group key is determined by scope and mode: daily → DATE(logged_at), year+aggregated → to_char(logged_at,'YYYY-MM'), month+aggregated → ISO week key, all_time+aggregated → to_char(logged_at,'YYYY'). WHERE clause restricts to the selected period. Returns rows keyed by bucket_id with summed metric values. NOTE: For scope=all_time+aggregated, this step must run before step 8 (compute_bucket_boundaries) because step 8 requires the db_rows result to enumerate the distinct years that form the bucket list.
outputs: dict mapping bucket_id → {kcal, protein_g, carbs_g, fat_g, fiber_g} from DB

internal_flow.name: zero_fill_and_build_rows (report)
internal_flow.description: Two conditional paths based on whether bucket_ids is empty or non-empty. Normal path (bucket_ids non-empty): for each bucket id in the ordered list from step 8, if the bucket id is present in the DB result use its values; otherwise emit a zero-value row. Attach bucket_label from the mapping computed in step 8. Passthrough path (bucket_ids empty — the all_time+daily case only): emit one row per entry in db_rows in ascending bucket_id order; derive bucket_label for each row as the day-of-month integer string extracted from the YYYY-MM-DD bucket_id (e.g., bucket_id '2025-03-07' → bucket_label '7'). Produce the final ordered list of Dataset rows where id=bucket_id.
inputs: ordered bucket id list (may be empty for all_time+daily)
outputs: ordered list of Dataset row dicts with id, bucket_label, kcal, protein_g, carbs_g, fat_g, fiber_g

internal_flow.name: build_report_dataset (report)
internal_flow.description: Wrap the row list in a Dataset using REPORT_SCHEMA and DatasetMeta(object_type='food_report_bucket', label=<human label for scope/period/mode>, total=len(rows), page=1, page_size=len(rows), row_actions=[]). Return HTTP 200.

Zero-fill: all five metric columns must be 0 (integer or float, consistent with DB rows) for buckets with no logged entries

period_key validation regex by scope: year=r'^\d{4}$', month=r'^\d{4}-\d{2}$', week=r'^\d{4}-W\d{2}$'

ui_implementer: Update src/shellConfig.ts: add { id: 'report', label: 'Report', path: '/food/report', order: 2 } to both mobilePrimaryNav and desktopNav. secondaryMenu remains empty. Do not change the existing log nav item.

Implement src/ReportPage.tsx as the top-level component for the /food/report route. ReportPage owns all page-level state: scope (string), period_key (string | null), mode ('aggregated' | 'daily'), navStack (array of {scope, period_key, mode} for back navigation), topMetric (string, default 'protein_g'), bottomMetric (string, default 'kcal'), currentDataset (Dataset | null), isLoading (boolean), error (ApiError | null).

ReportPage fetches GET /api/food/report with the current scope/period_key/mode on mount (default: scope=month, period_key=current YYYY-MM, mode=daily) and on any scope, mode, or drill/back navigation change. Metric changes within the current dataset must not trigger a new fetch.

ReportPage renders: a scope selector (all_time | year | month | week), a mode selector (aggregated | daily; hidden when scope=week), a back button (visible and enabled when navStack is non-empty), two vertically stacked chart panels each containing a metric selector and a BarChart.

The scope selector always navigates to the system-current period for the selected scope (e.g. selecting 'month' sets period_key to the current YYYY-MM). Selecting from the scope selector clears navStack.
The back button pops from navStack and navigates to the previous scope/period_key/mode, triggering a fetch.

Drill navigation: clicking a bar column in either chart in aggregated mode pushes the current scope/period_key/mode onto navStack and navigates to the drilled period. Drill target by current scope: all_time→year (period_key=clicked bucket id as YYYY), year→month (period_key=clicked bucket id as YYYY-MM), month→week (period_key=clicked bucket id as YYYY-WNN). Drill is not available in daily mode.

Each chart panel renders a BarChart (recharts BarChart or equivalent) with x=bucket_label, y=<selected metric key>, using the rows from the current Dataset. Each chart panel's metric selector is independent local state within the panel.
Metric selector options in display order: Protein (protein_g), Calories (kcal), Carbohydrates (carbs_g), Fat (fat_g), Fiber (fiber_g). Duplicate metric selection across the two panels is permitted.
y-axis scaling is independent per chart — do not share a y-axis domain between the two panels.
Render Skeleton while isLoading=true. Render ErrorCard if error is non-null. Render both chart panels from the same Dataset rows.
Material 3 page structure and controls apply. Chart library visual decisions are deferred to the implementer — recharts is available.
Mode selector is hidden (not disabled) when scope=week.
Do not implement prefetch, background loading, or any caching beyond React component state retained during the page session.

risks.risk: kcal rounding discrepancy between preview and insert (Sprint 01 carry-over)
risks.impact: If the application layer rounds differently from the DB NUMERIC(7,0) truncation, the preview value shown to the user may differ from what is stored. Mitigation: always apply Python int(round(kcal)) before preview and before insert.

risks.risk: good_fat_g > fat_g or red_meat_g > meat_g after rounding (Sprint 01 carry-over)
risks.impact: Floating-point rounding could cause a value pair that passes application-layer validation to trigger a DB CHECK constraint. Mitigation: enforce the constraint in the application validator before insert.

risks.risk: tools.py psycopg3 import present in same package (Sprint 01 carry-over)
risks.impact: If tools.py is imported at module level anywhere in the backend package, the Docker image build may fail or wrong host resolution may be exercised. Mitigation: backend package is self-contained under backend/; tools.py must not be imported.

risks.risk: ISO week boundary crossing month boundary
risks.impact: A week in the month+aggregated view may start in the previous month or end in the next month. The bucket generation logic must use ISO week semantics consistently with the WHERE clause to avoid mismatched or missing rows. Implementer must verify that the week bucket ids produced in step 8 match exactly the group keys produced in step 9.

risks.risk: all_time scope with no data returns an empty Dataset
risks.impact: If foodtracker.food_logs has no rows, all_time+aggregated returns zero rows. The frontend must handle an empty rows array without error. Zero-fill only applies within a defined period; all_time with no data cannot define a period to fill.

risks.risk: Metric switching triggers refetch due to incorrect state dependency
risks.impact: If the frontend wires topMetric or bottomMetric into the useEffect dependency array that triggers the fetch, metric changes will refetch unnecessarily and degrade UX. The fetch effect must depend only on scope, period_key, and mode.
